rationale.text: The test has one requirement with three routes for each function of a temporal media: the function itself can be activated with the keyboard and with any pointing device, another function in the page performs the same action and can, or, where focus handling is too complex for the usual keys, documented working keyboard shortcuts perform it (the glossary note on keyboard access). The glossary defines activable as triggering the action with a pointer press or the Enter key, other keys such as arrows being allowed for sliders. Deciding this needs a keyboard pass and judgment. Which elements are the functions of a media player is not marked in the code, and the native controls of audio and video elements are drawn by the browser outside the page's DOM. Whether another function in the page performs the same action, and whether shortcuts are documented, needs reading. So even a control that cannot be activated by keyboard is not a mechanical fault: an equivalent may exist elsewhere. No axe rule is tagged for this test and no check is registered, so there are no links and the entry stays at none. The check custom/7-3-handler-not-focusable, registered for 7.3.1, finds elements with pointer or key listeners that are not in the focus order; it is not linked, because it does not know whether an element is a function of a media, and its fault says nothing about the equivalent-function and shortcut routes. Applicability is judgment: whether an element is a temporal media with control functions cannot be decided from the markup with certainty. Needs lists keyboard, because the methodology asks whether each function can be activated by keyboard, and state, because player controls often appear only on hover or focus.
